title: Magnifying dock navigation presented as a website component (Osmo Nr. 003)
attribution_visible_in_image: Visible text: 'Osmo' wordmark, 'osmo.supply', 'Nr. 003 / Apple Dock Navigation Bar', 'Clone in Webflow'. Likely the publisher; creator not confirmed.
contains_third_party_content: Brand logos (Notion, Asana, Slack, Spotify, Webflow, Adobe apps, Figma, etc.) are shown as tiles.

observed.layout: A pale strip holds a row of 11 square app-style tiles; the hovered 'Webflow' tile is enlarged, shows a hand cursor and a white tooltip label above it. Page chrome: 'Osmo' wordmark with an asterisk top-left, '-> osmo.supply' top-right, footer 'Nr. 003 / Apple Dock Navigation Bar' bottom-left and a 'Clone in Webflow' button bottom-right.
observed.hierarchy: The hovered tile is the only enlarged, labeled item.
observed.typography: Small grotesk UI type, dark on warm grey. Unconfirmed.
observed.materials: Flat; the strip is almost the same color as the page.

interpretation.aesthetic: Component-library presentation of a macOS-dock hover-magnification effect used as website navigation.
implementation_notes: Magnification: distance-based scale of the hovered tile and its neighbors (pointer tracking in JS or sibling selectors).
Tooltip appears above the hovered tile.
The 'Clone in Webflow' button indicates it is built with Webflow interactions.
interpretation.caveat: Motion is not visible; inferred from the title and the hovered state.

concept_work.essence: Borrow the desktop dock's playful magnification to make a navigation row feel tactile.
what_makes_it_work: Label appears only where attention is.
Uniform tile size keeps the row orderly.
gaps_to_make_it_work: Labels are hover-only; no keyboard focus or touch equivalent shown.
Strip barely separates from the page.

pattern.name: Magnifying dock navigation
use_when: Desktop portfolios or showcase sites with up to about 12 icon-recognizable destinations
must_preserve: Label on hover and on keyboard focus
adaptation_examples: Agency portfolio: tiles are case-study thumbnails.
Developer docs: dock of integrations with focus labels.

lessons: Hover-driven delight needs keyboard and touch equivalents before it can be shipped.
Define the container: a component with no visible boundary reads as floating icons.

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: Neutral warm-grey stage; all chroma comes from third-party logo tiles.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: The component's job (navigate between a set of tools) and its clone-ready packaging are clear.
Clean and spacious but the strip has almost no contrast with the page, weakening the container.
Dock magnification is a desktop-OS metaphor; labels, focus and touch behavior are not addressed.
Only the hover state is shown; no active, focus, touch or overflow states.
Uniform tile size, radius and spacing across the row.
Applying the OS dock to site navigation is a distinctive, motion-led idea.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 8.5:1; secondary text min 2.53:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
